title: Choose the visual world for setebaidservices.org
question: The roll assigned The Dining-Hall Board. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Dining-Hall Board
options.lineage: the chalk board in a camp dining hall: today's schedule, menu, mail call, birthdays, with paper notices and photos pinned around it
options.thesis: The homepage is the board every camper reads at breakfast: what is happening now, which camp is yours, what it costs, and where to sign up.
options.viewport: A full-width green board. Top line in chalk: the season state and its deadline (for example 'Summer 2027 registration is open. Late fee after May 15.'). Below it, one enormous chalk headline: 'Summer camp for kids who just happen to have diabetes.' One chalk arrow line runs from that headline down through three pinned paper cards: Ages 7 to 13 (HDYC), Ages 13 to 17 (Camp Setebaid), Families (Family Conference), each with dates and a 'This is my camp' link. A pinned Polaroid strip of real camp photos (labelled placeholder until the real photos land) sits to the right with the camp video pinned under it. In the board's bottom corner, chalked small: 'Tier I to IV pricing. Every family pays what it can. Every child gets the same camp.'
options.risk: Reads as a cafe menu or a classroom if the lettering is generic; the board must be a camp dining hall, with pinned notices, Polaroids and the year, or it collapses into the chalkboard cliche. Long reading on a dark ground tires eyes, so body content lives on pinned paper, not on chalk.

raised.raise: One governing chalk line rules the composition: it runs from the season notice through the age picker to the register link, and every section hangs off that line, not off a card grid.

The season has named states (registration open, late-fee window, camp in session, after camp, event season) and exactly one element on the page changes to mark the state: the chalk date line. No scattered badges.
Hierarchy by scale contrast alone: the chalk headline is enormous, labels are tiny, and there are no decorative chalk doodles as filler.

options.label: The Camp Map
options.lineage: the hand-painted bird's-eye map on plywood at the camp entrance: cabins, lake, dining hall, nurse's cabin, archery range
options.thesis: The homepage is the painted map of camp, and each place on it answers a parent's question: the two age camps are two cabin rows, the nurse's cabin is the medical team, the camp store is the cost.
options.viewport: A painted map of Camp Mount Luther fills the viewport. A wooden signpost at the entrance carries the season state and three routed arrows: Ages 7 to 13, Ages 13 to 17, Families. Tapping an arrow pans the map to that camp's cabins and opens its dates, cost and register link. The nurse's cabin, dining hall and camp store are labelled stops.
options.risk: The most familiar of my candidates: illustrated camp maps are a known camp-world device, and the whole page depends on one large authored illustration that must be produced and kept accurate. Also the direction most runs in this category land on.

options.label: Boarding Pass and Gate Board
options.lineage: a segmented boarding pass beside a live gate board that reranks by departure time
options.thesis: Every program is a departure row: date, ages, cost, status. A changed deadline lights up and stays lit until you have seen it.
options.viewport: A board of program rows ordered by date: HDYC July 11 to 17 ages 7 to 13, Camp Setebaid July 11 to 17 ages 13 to 17, Family Conference, Setebaid Walk. Each row carries status: Open, Late fee after May 15, Full, Done. The parent's boarding pass to the right: child's age in, matching camp out.
options.case: Fuses cleanly: dates, ages, cost and status in ranked rows is the clearest possible answer to 'when, what, how much'. Loses on identification: parents sending a child to a lake in Mifflinburg do not see an airport.
options.risk: Cold. The offer is clear but the warmth, friends and fun that make a parent trust the place have no room in a departures grid.

options.label: Camp Shirt Screenprint
options.lineage: translucent spot-colour screenprint with registration drift
options.thesis: The homepage is this year's camp shirt: flat spot colours, one poster line, the year, and the print slipping half a step out of register when it moves.
options.viewport: A white sheet with 'SETEBAID SUMMER 2027' in stencil caps across the top in one ink, campers massed as flat cyan and scarlet shapes, and the three camps as three overprinted colour blocks whose overlaps name the ages. The season state prints in the margin like a registration mark.
options.case: Holds identification: every camper and alum owns a camp shirt, and teens will see themselves. Roughly even on clarity: a poster line carries the offer, but the age pick and cost need care to stay readable inside the overprint.
options.risk: Reads as a print-shop demo when the drift is decorative; the overlap must do work (the ages overlap, the tiers overlap) or it is a costume.

options.label: Split-Flap Concourse Board
options.lineage: a rail concourse split-flap departures board at rush hour
options.thesis: The camp calendar as a split-flap board: rows ranked by date, and when registration opens or a deadline passes, the letters clack over one by one.
options.viewport: A black board with white condensed caps: HDYC, CAMP SETEBAID, FAMILY CONFERENCE, WALK, each with date, ages, and status flaps. The season change is a cascade of flips across the top row. Below the board, paper: the offer and the age picker.
options.case: Holds clarity: time-ranked rows with per-character state change make 'what is happening now' impossible to miss. Loses identification: strict flap cells refuse warm copy and photos, and a black steel board is far from a lake in July.
options.risk: Novelty. Once the flaps have flipped, the grammar has nothing more to say to a parent reading about medical care and cost.

options.label: Curved-Crease Paper Shell
options.lineage: a circular sheet folded along one sweeping curved crease
options.thesis: One arc rules the page and lifts a flat sheet into a rigid form.
options.viewport: A cream disc lifting along one charcoal arc, labels in geometer's italic.
options.case: Fuses poorly: parents of a child with diabetes do not identify with paper geometry, and an arc-ruled sheet hides the offer and the action.
options.kept: Layout ruled by one governing line rather than a rectangular grid.

options.label: Rain-Night Cityscape
options.lineage: a cityscape passing from blue hour into rain-dark night and first dawn
options.thesis: Camp at night: cabin lights, a campfire, and the 2 a.m. check the parent no longer has to do.
options.viewport: A dark nocturne shifting by hour, one element marking the time.
options.case: Fuses poorly: a dark urban nocturne is foreign to a rural Pennsylvania camp for children, and shifting the hour is a gimmick against the offer. It loses both axes.
options.kept: Named time states, and exactly one element that changes to mark the state.
options.risk: Dark and moody on a page that must feel like July.

options.label: Variable Type Specimen
options.lineage: an interactive type specimen with a live axis slider
options.thesis: One giant word: drag the slider and DIABETES turns around into SETEBAID.
options.viewport: A single enormous letterform filling the screen with a slider under it.
options.case: The name story is real and campers chose it, but a giant word hides the camps, the dates and the cost, and only type enthusiasts identify with a specimen. It loses both axes.
options.kept: Hierarchy by scale contrast alone, no ornament.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The summer-camp website every camp ships: full-bleed photo of kids at the lake, a slogan, three cards, a quote, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: A full-bleed camp photo with the slogan and a Register button, then three cards: Camps, Donate, Volunteer.
canonCard.risk: Interchangeable with every other camp site by design, and the anti-goal you named.
